title: Anointing
lead: Pouring olive oil on a person or object to set it apart for God: priests, kings, sometimes prophets, and the tabernacle and its furniture. A king was "the LORD's anointed" (mashiach), the root of the word Messiah.

sections.b: Jacob pours oil on the stone at Bethel (Genesis 28:18). Moses anoints Aaron and his sons and the tabernacle with a holy oil no one else may copy (Exodus 30:22–33; Leviticus 8:10–12). Samuel anoints Saul with a flask and David with a horn of oil, and with David's anointing the Spirit of the LORD comes on him (1 Samuel 10:1; 1 Samuel 16:13). Because the king was "the LORD's anointed," David refuses to harm Saul (1 Samuel 24:6). Elijah is told to anoint Elisha (1 Kings 19:16), and the servant of Isaiah 61:1 is anointed by the Spirit, words Jesus reads of himself (Luke 4:18). The church's practice of anointing the sick with oil comes from James 5:14.
